title: Events & Game Modes
description: Time-limited events plus the recurring game modes heroes are rated for. Modes below are stubs built from hero-guide context; expand as we map each one live.
sources: Kingshot Optimizer hero guides (context), shared by user

entries.name: Expedition
entries.summary: Mode where heroes' Expedition skills apply (often passive/global growth or gathering bonuses). Heroes carry a separate 'Expedition' skill set from their Conquest one.

entries.name: Conquest
entries.summary: Stage-based combat mode; heroes use their active 'Conquest' skills. Clearing Conquest stages increases account (idle) income. Distinct from Arena. See resources.json for the idle-income claim flow.

entries.name: Arena
entries.summary: Champion PvP combat mode. A hero's Arena ability is rated SEPARATELY from its Conquest ability — different events lean on one or the other.

entries.name: Bear Hunt
entries.summary: Rally event against a Bear boss; heroes serve as Bear Rally Lead or Bear Joiner. Troop ratios matter for damage. Growth-only heroes (e.g. Olive) should NOT be used here — they waste combat slots.

best_formation.note: Bear is archer-heavy: shift almost everything to archers as generations progress.

rally_leaders_by_generation.note: Recommended rally-lead trios per generation from the Bear guide (external source). Spelling normalized to our roster where safe: 'Merlin'=Marlin, 'Fahad'=Fahd. 'Seo-yul' is not in our current roster (left as-is).

not_work: Moose pet — reduces enemy squad Health, but the Bear has no Health bar (only Defense), so it does nothing

instant_fill_solution.goal: Even troop split so every joiner slot fills the rally without overshoot.
steps: Subtract the Rally Leader's Squad Capacity (e.g. 162,210).
Divide by the 14 available joiner slots (970,000 / 14 = 69,285).
Round to a clean figure: ~69,000 troops per joiner.

joiner_tier_list.note: Tier list DERIVED FROM our Bear Joiner star ratings in knowledge/hero_event_ratings.json (source of truth), mapped S=5, A=4, B=3, C=2, Trash=1. See reconciliation_vs_external_guide for where the external Bear guide disagreed.

reconciliation_vs_external_guide.note: External Bear guide's joiner tiers differed from our ratings on 6 heroes. Per decision, our ratings win; differences recorded here for reference. Guide only covered up to Gen 5 (did not cover Eric/Yang/Triton/Sophia/Ava/Charles/Wee & Woo).
reconciliation_vs_external_guide.diana_note: Diana is purely an economy hero — Trash for Bear joining in both sources.

entries.name: Strongest Governor
entries.summary: A multi-stage scoring event with daily milestones, per-stage rankings and an overall ranking. This entry separates guaranteed rewards from ranking rewards and gives a value-priority framework for deciding whether to spend saved resources on a points push.

reward_buckets.how_earned: Reach stage point thresholds during the active day.
reward_buckets.best_use: Best baseline target for F2P and low-spend accounts.

reward_buckets.how_earned: Place high during a specific stage.
reward_buckets.best_use: Worth considering when your saved items match the stage perfectly.

reward_buckets.how_earned: Hold a high total score across the event.
reward_buckets.best_use: Only chase if you can fund multiple stages without breaking future plans.

reward_buckets.how_earned: Complete routine event tasks and claim available chests.
reward_buckets.best_use: Low-risk value for every active account.

reward_value_priority.values_most: Accounts replacing or starring core march heroes.
reward_value_priority.priority_note: High value when the hero fits your current generation and troop role.
Better when the next gear breakpoint changes a real march.
Good if you can recycle them into a stronger future event.
Useful, but rarely worth overpaying for ranking alone.
Do not let cosmetic value drive a bad points push.

when_ranking_worth_chasing: You already planned to complete the same upgrades for account progression.
Your saved inventory covers the target bracket without emergency packs.
The reward includes materials you cannot get efficiently elsewhere.
The event overlaps with KVK, Alliance Brawl, or another scoring window.
notes: If you need to buy the last bracket without knowing the final leaderboard pace, treat the reward as speculation, not planning.

entries.name: Swordland Showdown
entries.summary: An alliance PvP event decided by objective TIMING and coverage, not by raw brawling volume. Alliances underperform when they fight everywhere and plan too little; the event rewards focused pressure that lands on the right targets during the windows that actually swing the score.

details.core_idea: Won by the alliance that knows which windows matter, not the busiest one. Unfocused pressure 'leaks' value (e.g. strong players tied up in a low-value lane while a key window opens elsewhere).
key_levers: Window ownership: explicitly assign who owns each objective window; unowned windows get dropped because everyone assumes someone else has it.
Launch discipline: rallies that leave late or land staggered waste good rosters; synchronized launches convert cleaner.
Match plan to kingdom age: don't imitate mature-kingdom execution without the hero depth / march quality / War Academy maturity to back it.
Right leads: not every strong player should host every push; pick the best damage/survivability lead per window.
details.source: kingshotguide.com Swordland Showdown guide, shared by user (dated 2026-04-11)

entries.name: Viking Vengeance
entries.summary: Alliance PvE-style event where members rally shared Viking targets across a difficulty ladder. It is primarily an ALLIANCE EXECUTION check, not a solo power check: most missed rewards come from small collective mistakes stacking (wrong difficulty, sloppy start, poor rally timing) rather than one weak player.

details.difficulty_principle: The correct difficulty is the highest level the alliance can clear CLEANLY and REPEATEDLY, not the highest it can click.
details.reward_driver: Repeatable reward efficiency across the whole activity window beats one flashy push.
common_alliance_mistakes: Choosing difficulty by ego (highest they want to believe they can beat).
Starting without attendance discipline (too many members late = failed coordination, not lack of power).
Treating rally timing as an afterthought (late launches, messy joins, uneven landings cut efficiency).
Ignoring safe difficulty planning (not estimating a safe level first).
Not respecting recovery and repeatability (a clear that leaves the alliance unstable is not efficient).
external_tools_referenced: Rally Timer (standardize launch timing so members land together)
Castle Scheduler (map event window / leadership coverage)
